headline_marked: US and Iran [[begin peace talks in Switzerland]] amid high tension
headline: US and Iran begin peace talks in Switzerland amid high tension
summary: The 60-day summit in Bürgenstock aims to resolve disputes over nuclear programs and Lebanon, though Donald Trump has already issued fresh threats of strikes.
details: Peace talks between the US and Iran have officially begun in Bürgenstock, Switzerland, following a two-day delay. The 60-day summit aims to implement a 14-point memorandum of understanding to permanently end hostilities.

The US delegation is led by Vice President JD Vance, accompanied by special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Iran's delegation is led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.
Initial discussions focused on the release of frozen Iranian assets and the easing of sanctions on Iran's energy sector, specifically oil and petroleum products.

The talks are being mediated by Qatar and Pakistan. Pakistan's President Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Asim Munir are attending, alongside Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.
Tensions remain high as Iranian representatives reportedly refused to shake hands or take photos with the US delegation before the meetings started.
Despite the diplomatic effort, US President Donald Trump warned on Truth Social that he would strike Iran even more harshly if Tehran fails to stop Iranian-backed groups in Lebanon.
The talks were delayed due to ongoing Israeli attacks in Lebanon, which Iran cited as a primary reason for the initial hesitation to begin the summit.
caption:
US and Iran are finally face-to-face in Switzerland, but the atmosphere is frosty. No handshakes, no photos, and fresh threats of war.

Peace talks between the US and Iran have officially begun in Bürgenstock, Switzerland, following a two-day delay. The 60-day summit aims to implement a 14-point memorandum of understanding to permanently end hostilities.

The US delegation is led by Vice President JD Vance, accompanied by special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Iran's delegation is led by Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Initial discussions focused on the release of frozen Iranian assets and the easing of sanctions on Iran's energy sector, specifically oil and petroleum products.

The talks are being mediated by Qatar and Pakistan. Pakistan's President Shehbaz Sharif and Army Chief Asim Munir are attending, alongside Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani.

Tensions remain high as Iranian representatives reportedly refused to shake hands or take photos with the US delegation before the meetings started.

Despite the diplomatic effort, US President Donald Trump warned on Truth Social that he would strike Iran even more harshly if Tehran fails to stop Iranian-backed groups in Lebanon.

The talks were delayed due to ongoing Israeli attacks in Lebanon, which Iran cited as a primary reason for the initial hesitation to begin the summit.

headline_marked: 92% of Israelis believe [[Iran won the war]] and emerged stronger
headline: 92% of Israelis believe Iran won the war and emerged stronger
summary: A new poll shows overwhelming public sentiment in Israel that Iran gained more from the conflict and the subsequent deal with the US.
details: A poll of 3,644 respondents conducted by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the Agam Institute reveals that 92.1% of Israelis believe Iran won or gained more from the Middle East conflict.
The survey indicates that 82.9% of participants feel Israel's long-term security has been weakened, reflecting a stark shift in public sentiment.
Even among supporters of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc, 93.1% believe that Iran emerged as the victor in the conflict.
Public confidence in leadership is plummeting, with 72.5% of respondents stating they do not believe Netanyahu's claims about the military campaign's achievements.
Support for Netanyahu's premiership has dropped significantly, from 40.5% in early March to 29.4% in June.
Despite the internal crisis, 48.2% of respondents still support renewed major military action against Hezbollah in Lebanon, even at the risk of confronting Washington.
Meanwhile, negotiations to turn a temporary Iran-US agreement into a permanent deal are ongoing in Switzerland, amid continued tensions in Lebanon.
caption:
92% of Israelis believe Iran won the war. A new poll reveals a massive crisis of confidence in Israel's leadership.

A poll of 3,644 respondents conducted by the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the Agam Institute reveals that 92.1% of Israelis believe Iran won or gained more from the Middle East conflict.

The survey indicates that 82.9% of participants feel Israel's long-term security has been weakened, reflecting a stark shift in public sentiment.

Even among supporters of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc, 93.1% believe that Iran emerged as the victor in the conflict.

Public confidence in leadership is plummeting, with 72.5% of respondents stating they do not believe Netanyahu's claims about the military campaign's achievements.

Support for Netanyahu's premiership has dropped significantly, from 40.5% in early March to 29.4% in June.

Despite the internal crisis, 48.2% of respondents still support renewed major military action against Hezbollah in Lebanon, even at the risk of confronting Washington.

Meanwhile, negotiations to turn a temporary Iran-US agreement into a permanent deal are ongoing in Switzerland, amid continued tensions in Lebanon.
